items.title: A 12-Year-Old Security Flaw Was Just the Beginning | Threat Wire
items.summary: How did a 12-year-old critical security vulnerability go undetected for so long—and why are flaws in GitLab, Node.js, and widely used software libraries putting so many systems at risk? In this episode of Hak5 Threat Wire, Ali Diamond breaks down a CVSS 10.0 GitLab vulnerability, a dangerous Brotli security flaw, a certificate authority shutdown, and a massive 10-terabyte data breach at PingCAP. Plus, discover how the Railway breach and a compromised LiteLLM Python package put developer credentials, API keys, and sensitive data at risk. items.title: Exposing Bad Consumer Crypto - AI vs. Encrypted Drives
items.summary: What happens when a 27-year-old gets handed the keys to completely refactor nearly all of Cisco’s code? This week’s episode dives into tech’s strangest management bets and the friction brewing inside one of the industry’s giants. • Cisco gives a 27-year old the task of recoding 98% of their software with AI. • A serious but not earth shaking vulnerability found in PXE booting. • The largest ($6.3 BILLION) financial heist in history (with crypto). • 710 Polymarket gambling wallets emptied of $2.7 million. • A new robots.txt control for AI bots, and agreement to obey it. • Google generates haiku from the first orbital AI. • From our listeners: Does stealth updating make sense, how to move web servers off the Internet, books don't contain knowledge, a small company attacked by powerful AI, how would an "AI kill switch" be implemented. • Another new and worrisome application of reverse-engineering AI Show Notes - https://www.grc.com/sn/SN-1103-Notes.pdf Hosts: Steve Gibson and Mikah Sargent Security Now episode 1103 More Info: https://twit.tv/shows/security-now/episodes/1103 Sponsors: • http://hoxhunt.com/securitynow • http://threatlocker.com/twit • http://trustedtech.team/twit • http://bitwarden.com/twit Download or subscribe to Security Now at https://twit.tv/shows/security-now You can submit a question to Security Now at the GRC Feedback Page.
